summary: The facelifted (MY27) Q4 e-tron is Audi's MEB-platform medium electric SUV, and for now only the 250kW dual-motor quattro is orderable in Australia, as an SUV and a lower-roofed Sportback, ahead of first deliveries in the first half of 2027. Australian reviewers who drove it overseas praise the improved cabin quality, refined ride, rear-seat room and boot, but call its 400V charging and handling merely average and say it carries a clear premium over related Volkswagen Group EVs. The range is deliberately thin for now: the old 45 and 55 grades are running out, and the cheaper rear-drive 150kW model (priced at $71,650 for both bodies) has no order date yet, so it is not listed here.
pros: Price cuts of up to $18,168 put both quattro grades ($81,650 SUV, $83,250 Sportback) under the $91,661 luxury-car-tax and FBT-exemption threshold, which the outgoing 55 quattro exceeded
Usable 77kWh battery (82kWh gross) gives 494km WLTP in the SUV and 509km in the Sportback on 20-inch wheels, with DC charging up to 185kW and 10-80 per cent in about 27 minutes
Braked towing rises to 1,800kg on quattro models in Audi's facelift data, up 400kg and level with a VW ID.5 GTX
Practical for its footprint: 515L (SUV) and 527L (Sportback) boots, with reviewers singling out rear legroom and headroom
5-year unlimited-km warranty with 8 years/160,000km on the high-voltage battery, and orders placed in 2026 include a six-year/90,000km service plan
cons: Both quattro grades sit above the $75,000 cap that applies to the novated-lease FBT exemption from 1 April 2027, whereas both Cupra Tavascan grades and most Skoda Enyaq grades on the same platform list under it
Still dearer than the mechanically related Skoda Enyaq RS ($76,590) and VW ID.5 GTX ($72,990), and CarExpert finds the steering short on feel and the dynamics inert
400V architecture keeps peak DC charging at 185kW, which Chasing Cars calls nothing special against faster-charging rivals
Reviewers note harder rear door trims, a driver display with a large bezel and fewer customisation options, the loss of physical climate controls and no frunk for cables
Not delivered until the first half of 2027, and Audi has not confirmed Australian-specification towing or boot figures, so the 1,800kg tow rating is from international data
